property_summary: Only the contract owner can successfully call AdjustBetAmounts (calls by non-owner revert).
Only the contract owner (deployer) can successfully call AdjustBetAmounts; calls from any address that is not the owner must revert when attempting AdjustBetAmounts.
Only the contract owner (the deployer of C) can successfully call AdjustBetAmounts; calls from any caller other than the original deployer must revert.
If the caller is not the contract owner, calling AdjustBetAmounts must revert (i.e., only the owner can successfully call AdjustBetAmounts).

For every caller address X and bet amount A, in the reference contract only the owner (deployer) can successfully call AdjustBetAmounts(A) (i.e. the call does not revert and betLimit becomes A); the mutant which changes onlyOwner to require whale instead of owner will reject (or otherwise not set betLimit for) some callers X (notably the deployer) so there exist inputs where AdjustBetAmounts succeeds on reference but fails or leaves betLimit unchanged on the mutant.

For every caller address A and value V, the reference contract allows the deployer (owner) to call AdjustBetAmounts(V) and updates betLimit to V; the mutant changes onlyOwner to require whale instead of owner, so when the deployer is not the whale some inputs (caller A = deployer) will be unable to change betLimit or the call will revert, breaking the rule.

For all uint256 newLimit and caller addresses, the contract allows the deployer (owner) to successfully call AdjustBetAmounts(newLimit) (i.e., the call does not revert and betLimit becomes newLimit); the mutant that requires whale instead of owner prevents the deployer from performing this for some inputs, so there exist inputs where AdjustBetAmounts either reverts or leaves betLimit unchanged.

For every uint256 newLimit, the contract's deployer (owner) can successfully call AdjustBetAmounts(newLimit) and after the call c.currentBetLimit() == newLimit; the mutant that requires whale instead of owner breaks this because when the deployer != whale the call will fail or leave betLimit unchanged for some inputs.

For every uint256 newLimit the deployer (owner) can call AdjustBetAmounts(newLimit) and c.currentBetLimit() equals newLimit afterward; the mutant requiring whale instead of owner causes some calls (when deployer != whale) to either revert or leave betLimit unchanged, violating this rule.
Only the contract owner can change difficulty via AdjustDifficulty (calling AdjustDifficulty by msg.sender != owner must not change currentDifficulty).

property_summary: Only the original owner address can successfully call AdjustDifficulty (calls by other addresses revert), so AdjustDifficulty reverts whenever msg.sender is not the contract's owner.
If the current caller is NOT the owner, AdjustDifficulty must revert.
If the current caller is not the contract owner, calls to AdjustDifficulty by that caller must revert (the test asserts AdjustDifficulty reverts).
AdjustDifficulty reverts for the current caller (i.e., non-owner callers cannot successfully call AdjustDifficulty).

For every caller X and any input value, calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) from X on the reference contract never changes the difficulty (difficulty remains what it was); the mutant flips onlyOwner to require msg.sender != owner so some caller(s) can cause AdjustBetAmounts to succeed while also being able to call AdjustDifficulty (or vice-versa) and thereby produce a differing difficulty after an AdjustBetAmounts call in some executions, violating the invariant that AdjustBetAmounts never changes difficulty.

For every caller and input, calling AdjustBetAmounts(...) does not change the contract's difficulty; the mutant changes onlyOwner to require msg.sender != owner so some caller can both call AdjustBetAmounts and (due to altered access) cause difficulty to differ, violating this invariant.

For all callers and inputs, calling AdjustBetAmounts(...) does not change the contract's difficulty (difficulty stays equal to its prior value); the mutant flips onlyOwner to require msg.sender != owner which allows some caller to successfully invoke AdjustBetAmounts when the reference wouldn't, causing difficulty to differ after the call for some inputs.

For every caller and input, calling AdjustBetAmounts(uint256) does not change the contract's difficulty (the difficulty getter value remains equal to its pre-call value); the mutant flipping onlyOwner to require msg.sender != owner allows a different caller to succeed and thus can change difficulty in some executions, violating this invariant.

For every caller and input, calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) does not change the contract's difficulty (difficulty remains equal to its pre-call value); the mutant flips onlyOwner to require msg.sender != owner which allows some caller to pass the modifier when the original would not, enabling a sequence that changes difficulty and thus violating this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller who is the contract owner, calling OpenToThePublic() results in openToPublic becoming true in the reference contract, whereas the mutant flips it to false — so the property is that after an owner call OpenToThePublic(), c.currentlyOpen() (via a public view of the boolean) is true for all inputs; the mutant will make it false for some input (the owner call).

For any owner who calls OpenToThePublic(), the contract's openToPublic flag becomes true in the reference implementation; the mutant flips it to false, so there exist inputs (an owner call) where the mutant violates this rule.

After the contract owner calls OpenToThePublic(), the contract's openToPublic boolean becomes true for every admissible owner call in the reference; the mutant flips it to false, so some owner calls will make the property false.

For any owner caller and any prior openToPublic state, after calling OpenToThePublic() the reference implementation guarantees openToPublic == true (observable via a public view through wager permissions), whereas the mutant sometimes leaves it false (so a subsequent action gated by isOpenToPublic will fail); the test fuzzes an arbitrary address as the caller and asserts that when the caller is the owner, OpenToThePublic enables public actions (wager) on the reference but the mutant will break this for some fuzzed inputs.

For any call to OpenToThePublic made by the contract owner, the reference contract sets the openToPublic flag to true (so a subsequent public-only action like donate succeeds), whereas the mutant flips the flag to false causing that subsequent public-only action to revert or fail; the test fuzzes an arbitrary donor address and donation amount to expose this difference.

For any caller who is the owner, invoking OpenToThePublic() on the correct contract sets openToPublic to true; the mutant (no-op) leaves openToPublic unchanged so there exist inputs (the owner caller) for which the property fails.
